lessons.title: What makes a good team
lessons.html:
Teams on the farm

Most farm work is done in teams: a picking team in the orchard, a dipping team at the dip tank, a shed team packing fruit, or a fencing team in the camps. A team is a group of people working together towards the same goal. When the team works well, the job is faster, safer and better. When it does not, work is repeated, people get hurt and tempers flare.

Roles in a team

Every team member has a role. In a dipping team, for example:

  • Some workers bring the cattle from the camp to the kraal.
  • Some work the crush and move animals forward.
  • One person counts animals and writes the record.
  • The team leader checks the dip and keeps everyone safe.

Know your own role and the roles of others. If one person does not do their part, others must cover, and the whole team slows down.

What good team members do

  • Arrive on time and ready to work.
  • Understand the team's goal for the day, for example to pick 20 bins or to dip 300 head.
  • Do their share of the work, including the hard parts.
  • Help others when they finish early or see someone struggling.
  • Follow the safety rules so they do not put others in danger.
  • Respect every member, whatever their age, gender, language or culture.

Team goals

The team leader or supervisor sets the goal. Make sure you understand it. Ask: What must we finish? By when? How good must the work be? If the goal seems impossible, say so politely and early, and explain why.

lessons.title: Communicating and solving problems together
lessons.html:
Talking and listening

Good communication keeps a team working together. Many problems start because someone did not understand an instruction or did not speak up.

  • Listen carefully when the leader explains the job.
  • Repeat back the main points to check you understood: So we start in block 6, row 1, and stop at the dam road?
  • Use clear, polite words. Shouting and swearing cause conflict.
  • Where team members speak different languages, use simple words, show with your hands, or ask someone to help translate.
  • Tell the team at once about danger, like a snake or a loose animal.

Giving and taking feedback

If a team member does something wrong, tell them calmly and privately, and explain how to do it right. If someone tells you that you made a mistake, listen, do not get angry, and fix it. Feedback helps everyone improve.

When there is conflict

People sometimes disagree. Conflict is normal, but it must be handled well.

  1. Stay calm. Do not fight or threaten.
  2. Talk to the person directly and listen to their side.
  3. Focus on the problem, not on the person.
  4. Look for a solution that is fair to both.
  5. If you cannot solve it, ask the team leader to help.

Solving work problems

When something goes wrong, such as a broken trailer during harvest, the team can solve it together. Tell the leader, share ideas, agree what to do and who will do it. For example, some workers keep picking into crates while the driver fetches another trailer.

Key points

  • A team works together towards one goal; every member has a role.
  • Do your share, help others and follow safety rules.
  • Listen, repeat back instructions and speak politely.
  • Handle conflict calmly and ask the leader for help if needed.
  • Solve problems together by sharing ideas and agreeing actions.
